rationale: This benchmark is a small (15 functions, ~7.3 KB text), arithmetic-heavy C++ program (BigInt/Fibonacci/Stepanov container loops) from SingleSource, so the dominant threats are pattern-matching on arithmetic idioms and control-flow recovery, while both runtime (benchmark timing) and code-size growth must stay bounded on a tiny baseline. SUB is weighted highest on SecurityGain because the BigInt and container code is dense in arithmetic/logic operations that instruction substitution obfuscates cheaply and near-risk-free; BCF and FLA follow to opaque the modest but non-trivial control flow in main, usage, and Fibonacci::get_number, with FLA's SizeCost slightly elevated since flattening inflates the already-largest functions (usage, main). SPLIT is kept with low cost weights as a cheap diversity amplifier that improves the efficacy of FLA/BCF on the few larger functions. IBR and ICALL get moderate security weights with suppressed RuntimeCost weights so the selector avoids applying indirect branching/calls to the hot numeric loops (mandel-text, stepanov iteration, BigInt multiply chains) where their per-call overhead would hurt most; ICALL's CorrectnessRisk is the highest in the table since rewriting call sites in C++ (vtables, exception edges) is the likeliest correctness hazard. IGV is retained at moderate weights to add global-data diversity across the five translation units at minimal cost. Overall, high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights favor broad application of the cheap, safe passes, while uniformly low RuntimeCost/SizeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights keep the selector from steering expensive or risky transformations toward the hot loops and the largest functions, preserving both performance and correctness within an acceptable envelope.
